angularDiameterSource: Computed here from the record's radius and distance: 2 x 171,281 km at 18.21 pc = 0.13 mas. No interferometric diameter of this star is used.
distanceSource: Gaia DR3 parallax 54.9036 +/- 0.0177 mas (same row, RUWE 1.26): 18.21 pc, no zero-point correction
radiusSource: Radius 0.2462 +/- 0.008 solar radii from August et al. 2025, the stellar radius of the default parameter set of LHS 1478 b in the NASA Exoplanet Archive (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2025A&A...695A.171A/abstract): 171,281 km at 695,700 km per solar radius. Mass 0.2301 +/- 0.0054 solar masses from August et al. 2025, the stellar mass of the default parameter set of LHS 1478 b in the NASA Exoplanet Archive (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2025A&A...695A.171A/abstract); GM is that mass times the JPL solar GM. Temperature 3415 +/- 82 K from August et al. 2025, the stellar temperature of the default parameter set of LHS 1478 b in the NASA Exoplanet Archive (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2025A&A...695A.171A/abstract). presentationUp: the display axis is a sky-plane convention; the spin axis's position angle on the sky is not measured.
effectiveTemperatureSource: August et al. 2025, the stellar temperature of the default parameter set of LHS 1478 b in the NASA Exoplanet Archive (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2025A&A...695A.171A/abstract)
surfaceGravitySource: log g from the mass and radius in packages/astronomy/data/bodies/lhs-1478.json (sources in its physicalNotes), log10(GM/R^2) in cgs: 5.017, rounded to two decimals
spectralTypeSource: NASA Exoplanet Archive, composite parameters of LHS 1478 (pscomppars): spectral type m3 V, from Soto et al. 2021 (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2021A&A...649A.144S/abstract)
metallicitySource: NASA Exoplanet Archive, composite parameters of LHS 1478 (pscomppars): [Fe/H] -0.38 dex, from August et al. 2025 (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2025A&A...695A.171A/abstract)
luminositySource: NASA Exoplanet Archive, composite parameters of LHS 1478 (pscomppars): log10 of the luminosity in solar units -2.1296, from August et al. 2025 (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2025A&A...695A.171A/abstract)
